analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture represents MakeMyTrip's next-generation Security Operations Center (SOC) platform. It ingests hybrid telemetry from public cloud (AWS) and on-premises infrastructure into an Apache Metron processing cluster running on EC2. Ingested events are parsed and enriched in real time. Persistent telemetry is batched and processed via Amazon EMR into Amazon S3 within a Security Data Lake, queryable by Amazon Athena for forensics and threat hunting, with long-term behavioral profiles fed back into Metron. Metron forwards alerts to a SOAR platform (Blitz on EC2), which notifies SOC analysts (ALERTS), who can trigger mitigation actions such as automated IP blocking on AWS WAF.

graph.name: MakeMyTrip Next-Gen SOC Architecture
graph.notes: Hybrid next-generation SOC ingesting 5,000 events/second from around 20 data sources and indexing ~250 million events per day in an AWS Security Data Lake.

nodes.name: AWS
nodes.notes: Public cloud telemetry source generating logs and events (e.g., S3, SNS, SQS, CloudTrail, GuardDuty).

nodes.name: ON-PREM
nodes.notes: On-premises telemetry source feeding logs via syslog or Apache Kafka.

nodes.name: APACHE METRON
nodes.notes: Central stream processing engine handling real-time log ingestion, parsing into JSON, contextual enrichment, and behavioral profiling.

nodes.name: EMR
nodes.notes: EMR jobs transforming persistent telemetry data from Metron into optimized storage formats for S3.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Central object storage for the serverless Security Data Lake, retaining months and years of telemetry events.

nodes.name: ATHENA
nodes.notes: Interactive SQL query service used for log analytics, threat mining, and digital forensics directly against S3.

nodes.name: SOAR
nodes.notes: Open-source Blitz SOAR framework on EC2 providing automated alert enrichment, reverse DNS, and Whois lookup.

nodes.name: ALERTS
nodes.notes: SOC analysts performing triage and incident response through a unified single-pane interface or Jira integration.

nodes.name: WAF
nodes.notes: Web Application Firewall used by analysts or automated workflows to mitigate threats by blocking malicious traffic sources.

edges.notes: Telemetry events from AWS public cloud services are pulled into Apache Metron.
On-premises log events are ingested into Apache Metron via syslog or Kafka.
Persistent telemetry data from Apache Metron is picked up by an EMR batch transformation job.
EMR writes processed telemetry data into S3 storage in the Security Data Lake.
Athena queries data stored in S3 for forensic investigation and analytics.
Long-term behavioral profiles and models generated from the Data Lake feed back to Metron for streaming enrichment.
Apache Metron forwards detection alerts to the Blitz SOAR platform.
SOAR presents enriched alerts to SOC analysts for investigation and triage.
SOC analysts trigger remediation and blocking rules on AWS WAF.
